title: daemon event loop wedge: synchronous git worktree add (distinct from the rerank spawn storm) evidence chunk 2
summary: 842ms transient lag here, though it can fully starve a CPU-constrained box per the other note); adding prepare produced the multi-second freeze. Fix (branch worktree-fix-daemon-sync-git-wedge): added async execFile variants to lib/git.js (createWorktreeAsync, removeWorktreeAsync, mergeBranchAsync, createFeatureWorktreeAsync, mergeFeatureAsync, removeFeatureWorktreeAsync, attemptDiffAsync, initRepoAsync, isRepoAsync, listWorktreesAsync; sync versions kept verbatim for CLI/tests) and made the already-async route handlers in routes/git.js, routes/task.js, routes/subconscious.js, routes/overlay.js await them. After the fix, /health stayed p50=4ms max=9ms while three real ~6s worktree adds ran concurrently (loop lagMax fell from ~6500-7400ms to ~184ms). Regression test test/git-async-nonblocking.test.js. Secondary, separate fix in the same branch: search-context rebuilt the whole graph once PER agentic round because the daemon ctx exposed no readGraphSnapshot — added an overlay-mtime-cached readGraphSnapshot so the graph builds once per request (measured latency climb 0.5s to 2.2s as the graph grew). The rerank/embed spawn-cooldown is intentionally NOT in this branch to avoid duplicatin
